The main takeaway from our work is that

the problem of learning a sparse linear model from corrupted observations is fundamentally easier than the problem of learning the same model from uncorrupted observations, in the sense that the former problem is learnable in polynomial time with a consistent estimator.
the presence of outliers in the data does not necessarily prevent us from learning the true parameters of the underlying distribution.
